title: A Once In A 100 Year Investment Opportunity Just Started (Most Aren’t Ready)
creator: Tom Nash
summary: Tom Nash's macro rebuttal of Michael Burry's crash warning is the video's spine. He lays out Burry's case — the market in 'stage one of grief' (denial, ~6-9 months, so a 2027 blow-up), puts on NVDA/PLTR/MU expiring through next year — then counters with data: the S&P 500 near record highs (~7,800, 30 record closes in 2026) yet priced at a forward P/E of ~19, exactly its 10-year average, with Q3 earnings growth near 30% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth implied. He walks through the risk ledger honestly — 10-year Treasury above 5.3% (highest since 2002, but the long-run average is ~5.5% and high-rate decades delivered the best equity returns), a Fed that hiked on 16 Sep into a hot economy, and Brent near $100 driven by Iran conflict capacity loss — and concludes each risk hits unprofitable, leveraged and rate-sensitive companies hardest, which are already on his avoid list, while net-cash compounders float. On Burry's AI-bubble thesis (chip depreciation stretched over 5-6 years, $3T in off-balance-sheet hyperscaler commitments), he cites Steve Eisman's counter: a cost problem only kills if revenues stop growing, and cloud backlogs are still surging. He admits bias upfront — he owns a lot of Palantir and Burry is shorting it — and uses Burry's Jan 2023 'sell' tweet (S&P ~4,077 then, ~7,800 now) as a market-timing cautionary tale. The playbook: emergency fund, DCA as normal, trim winners 10/20/30% at +50/+100/+150%, double down only below 10% off the 52-week high (7,040 for the S&P) or 20% for big growth names like PLTR/NVDA/TSLA. No new individual stock calls; consistent with his 2 Oct SPY core-holding stance. Also promoted his 17 Oct masterclass.
